answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a nectar as the anchor of the cost. A oasis stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a lantern...
